figures.caption: Figure 2: Overall retrieval trade-off across the six shared categories. Higher y-values indicate broader sensitivity; farther right indicates tighter alignment to the benchmark prompt under the subset relevance heuristic. Codex delivered the best balance, DeerFlow was the broadest useful expansion, and Biomni showed the largest but least specific output.
Table 1: System-level comparison of the three agent outputs as observed from the saved run folders.

Figure 4: Three-way accession overlap for the six shared benchmark categories in the run 2 crossagent comparison. Interior numbers report the seven Venn regions for each category, and the panel headers report total proteins retrieved by each agent in that category. Circle areas are schematic and are not proportional to set size.

Figure 3: Within-system run-to-run stability across the six shared prompt categories. C1–C6 follow the prompt order from inorganic-carbon acquisition through signaling and gene control. Codex was nearly invariant, DeerFlow was stable in the tighter transport categories but much less stable in signaling, and Biomni showed the largest run-to-run swings in the broadest bins.
Table 2: Category-level comparison across the six shared benchmark categories. Triple overlap is reported as a fraction of the union of all three systems for that category.

Figure 1: Benchmark workflow used in this study. Saved outputs from the three agent systems were normalized to UniProt accessions, reduced to the six shared prompt categories, and compared using overlap analysis plus a literature-informed relevance heuristic.
